decision_framework.title: Idempotency and Message Deduplication Strategy
decision_framework.context: Choosing the appropriate idempotency deduplication architecture across short-lived caching, transactional relational storage, and distributed event streams.

branch.condition: Stateless HTTP APIs with short mutation windows (e.g. payment checkout, external webhook ingesters)
branch.recommendation: Redis Distributed Lock + TTL Caching (24-48 hours) with Request Body Hash Comparison
branch.trade_offs: Sub-millisecond deduplication checks, automatic memory reclamation; trade-off: in rare Redis crash scenarios, key may be lost unless Redis AOF persistence is enabled.
branch.anti_pattern: Never store idempotency keys in local in-memory Node.js Maps in production; keys must be shared across all pods via Redis.

branch.condition: Mission-critical financial ledger, core banking transfers, and billing record creation
branch.recommendation: Database Unique Constraint on idempotency_key inside Transaction Table + In-Transaction Double Check
branch.trade_offs: Guarantees ACID atomicity with zero chance of lost keys; trade-off: slight database query overhead on initial check.
branch.anti_pattern: Never treat idempotencyKey as a decorative DTO field without querying the database for existing records before execution.

branch.condition: Asynchronous Event-Driven Microservices and Message Queues (Kafka / RabbitMQ)
branch.recommendation: Idempotent Consumer Pattern with Transactional Outbox and Message Deduplication Table
branch.trade_offs: At-least-once delivery safely converted into exactly-once processing semantics; trade-off: requires maintenance of message log cleanup jobs.
branch.anti_pattern: Never rely on messaging brokers alone to guarantee exactly-once delivery without consumer-side deduplication.
